2027-04-17.title: Saturday after the Second Sunday after Qyomtho
readings: By a single offering he has perfected for all time those who are sanctified
The great dinner: “Come; for everything is ready now”
2027-04-17.alt: Season of Qyomtho (the Resurrection), the week after the Second Sunday after the Resurrection. This evening the Third Sunday after the Resurrection begins with Evening Prayer; its Evening Gospel is Mark 16:9–13.
2027-04-17.verse: For by a single offering he has perfected for all time those who are sanctified.
theo: Christ is risen! The Letter to the Hebrews sets two pictures side by side. In the first, “every priest stands day after day at his service, offering again and again the same sacrifices that can never take away sins.” In the second, Christ “offered for all time a single sacrifice for sins” and “sat down at the right hand of God.” The priests of the old covenant stand, because their work is never finished. Christ sits, because his work is done: he died once, rose, and is enthroned with the Father. “For by a single offering he has perfected for all time those who are sanctified.” What, then, do we do at every Holy Qurbono? We do not add a new sacrifice to the Cross, and we do not repeat it as if it were incomplete. The one sacrifice of Calvary is made present on our altar, and the risen Lord who offered it once offers himself now through the ministry of the priest (Catechism 1366–1367). St John Chrysostom, preaching on this chapter, put it simply: we do not offer one lamb today and another tomorrow, but always the same; the sacrifice is one (in substance).

The Letter then calls the Holy Spirit as witness, quoting the prophet Jeremiah: “I will put my laws in their hearts, and I will write them on their minds,” and “I will remember their sins and their lawless deeds no more.” This is the new covenant: not a law carved on stone outside us, but the Spirit writing God's will inside us, and a forgiveness so complete that God himself chooses not to remember. The Gospel then opens a door to the feast. At a dinner someone exclaims, “Blessed is anyone who will eat bread in the kingdom of God!” Jesus answers with a parable. A man gave a great dinner and sent his servant to say, “Come; for everything is ready now.” But they all began to make excuses: a field, five yoke of oxen, a new marriage. None of these is a sin. They are good things put in the place of the invitation. The parable is not aimed at one people; the first disciples who accepted the invitation were themselves sons and daughters of Israel. It is a warning to every invited guest, and so to us. St Gregory the Great observed that the pleasures of the body, once possessed, soon weary us, but spiritual delights, once tasted, make us hungry for more (in substance).

The master then sends his servant into the streets and lanes for “the poor, the crippled, the blind, and the lame,” and again to the roads and lanes: “compel people to come in, so that my house may be filled.” The Church reads this “compel” as the urgency of love, never as force, for the act of faith must be given willingly (Catechism 160; Dignitatis Humanae 10). Tonight, as Saturday evening opens the Lord's Day, the invitation comes to us again: “Come; for everything is ready now.” Everything is ready at the Holy Qurbono tomorrow: the Word, the Body and Blood of the Lord, the peace of the risen Christ. What excuse is waiting in my week? A tuition class, a function, a site visit, tiredness? Prepare tonight. Make peace with someone, go to confession if you need to, plan to go as a family, and bring along one person who has stopped coming. The house is not yet full; there is still room.
outline: Ask: what excuse have I given God most often?
Point 1 · One sacrifice, for all time
The priests stand; Christ sits at the right hand.
Point 2 · Written on hearts, remembered no more
The new covenant of the Spirit and of forgiveness.
Point 3 · “Come; for everything is ready now”
The great dinner, the excuses, and the house still to be filled.
“By a single offering he has perfected for all time those who are sanctified.”
live: Plan tonight how your whole family will reach the Holy Qurbono tomorrow, and remove one excuse in advance.
Invite one person to come with you to church this Sunday, and offer to bring them.
2027-04-17.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, by one offering you have perfected for all time those who are sanctified, and now you sit at the right hand of the Father. Write your law on our hearts and remember our sins no more. You have prepared a great dinner and say to us, “Come; for everything is ready now.” Deliver us from every excuse that keeps us from your table, and send us into the streets and lanes to bring others with us, until your house is filled. You live and reign for ever. Amen.
altar: The Holy Qurbono is not a new sacrifice but the one sacrifice of the Cross made present, in which the risen Christ gives us his true Body and Blood; here the great dinner of the kingdom is already set before us.

quick: Christ offered one sacrifice for all time and sat down at God's right hand; the Holy Qurbono makes that one sacrifice present.
In the new covenant God writes his law on our hearts and remembers our sins no more.
God invites us: “Come; for everything is ready now”; we must not let good things become excuses.
2027-04-17.action: Name tonight one excuse that keeps you from God, and set it aside.
2027-04-17.question: Which good thing in my life has become an excuse for refusing God's invitation?

family.explain: A man prepared a big feast and invited many people. When the food was ready he sent his servant to call them. But they all gave excuses: “I bought a field,” “I bought some oxen,” “I just got married.” So the man invited poor and sick people instead, and there was still room! God invites us every Sunday to the Holy Qurbono. Everything is ready.
family.intention: We pray for those who will miss the Holy Qurbono tomorrow, that they may hear God's invitation.
family.ask: Ask: “What can we do tonight so that nothing stops us from going to church tomorrow?”

illus: A young software engineer in Thiruvananthapuram always had a reason for missing the Sunday Qurbono: a release deadline, a new flat to furnish, a cousin's wedding in another town. “Next Sunday,” he would tell his mother on the phone. One Saturday his nephew, who was preparing for his First Holy Communion, called and asked him to come and see him serve at the altar the next morning. He went, a little embarrassed. When the priest lifted up the holy gifts, he found himself thinking of the parable he had once learned in Sunday school: everything is ready now. That evening he went to confession for the first time in four years. He still has deadlines; he no longer lets them decide his Sundays.

pm.open: Christ is risen! Lord Jesus, you have prepared a feast for us and you call us by name. Make us glad to answer your invitation. Amen.
share: Christ had offered for all time a single sacrifice for sins (Hebrews 10:12). How does this change the way I take part in the Holy Qurbono?
I will remember their sins and their lawless deeds no more (Hebrews 10:17). Do I believe that God has truly forgiven me?
But they all alike began to make excuses (Luke 14:18). What are my usual excuses?
pm.resp: Lord, we come; your table is ready.
interc: For the Church, that her invitation may reach the streets and lanes of every town.
For those who have stopped coming to the Holy Qurbono, that they may hear the Lord's call again.
For the poor, the sick and the disabled, that they may find a place of honour at the Lord's table.
For families, that nothing may come before their Sunday worship together.
For all who carry the weight of past sins, that they may trust in God who remembers them no more.
pm.close: Father, your Son offered one sacrifice for all time, and you have set before us the great dinner of your kingdom. Write your law on our hearts, deliver us from every excuse, and fill your house with guests from every road and lane. Through Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, Christ is risen! The Letter to the Hebrews contrasts the priests who stand day after day offering the same sacrifices with Christ, who offered for all time a single sacrifice for sins and sat down at the right hand of God (Hebrews 10:12).

He sits because his work is finished. The Holy Qurbono does not add to the Cross; it makes the one sacrifice present, and the risen Lord gives himself to us. And in this new covenant God says: I will remember their sins and their lawless deeds no more.

In the Gospel a man gives a great dinner and says: Come; for everything is ready now (Luke 14:17). But the guests make excuses: a field, oxen, a marriage. Good things, put in the place of the invitation. So the master calls the poor, the crippled, the blind and the lame, and still there is room.
Tonight Sunday begins. Everything is ready for us tomorrow: the Word, the Body and Blood of Christ, his peace. Let us lay aside our excuses, prepare our hearts, and bring someone with us. Amen.
kids: Children, imagine someone made a huge feast with all your favourite food, and invited you, and you said: “Sorry, I'm busy.” In Jesus' story people said exactly that! So the man invited poor and sick people, and the house was filled. Every Sunday Jesus invites us to his feast, the Holy Qurbono. Will you say “Yes, I am coming!” tomorrow?

intro: Theme: “Come; for everything is ready now.”
On the Saturday before the Third Sunday after the Resurrection: the one sacrifice, the new covenant written on hearts, and the great dinner.

sub: The priests stand day after day.
Christ offered once and sat down.
The Holy Qurbono makes the one sacrifice present.
q: The Lord says to my lord, “Sit at my right hand until I make your enemies your footstool.”
The death he died, he died to sin, once for all; but the life he lives, he lives to God.
points.apply: At the Holy Qurbono tomorrow, unite your week, its work and its troubles, with the one offering of Christ.

points.h: Written on hearts, remembered no more
q: But this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days, says the Lord: I will put my law within them, and I will write it on their hearts; and I will be their God, and they shall be my people.
If we confess our sins, he who is faithful and just will forgive us our sins and cleanse us from all unrighteousness.
points.apply: If a past sin still weighs on you, confess it and then trust that God remembers it no more.

sub: A field, oxen, a marriage: good things as excuses.
The poor and the lame are brought in.
q: Ho, everyone who thirsts, come to the waters; and you that have no money, come, buy and eat!
Blessed are those who are invited to the marriage supper of the Lamb.
points.apply: Bring one person with you to the Holy Qurbono this Sunday.

concl: Christ's one sacrifice is complete, and it is made present for us at every Holy Qurbono.
God's table is ready; let no good thing become our excuse, and let us fill his house.
2027-04-17.resolve: Tonight, set aside one excuse and prepare your heart and your family for the Lord's Day.
